FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by~the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Rotating Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Engineering Division Council. This standard has beenprepared to specify the requirements for three-phase squirrel cage induction motors intended to be used for fans used in air-conditioning and ventilation. Fans covered in this standard may be classified into following two groups: i) Axial flow fans which produce a flow of air in a direction parallel to the axis of rotation. The axial flow fans are most commonly used for applications requiring flow against low resistances. These fans are applied in air-conditioning work. ii) Centrifugal fans which produce a flow perpendicular to the axis of rotation. Centrifugal fans may have either straight radial blades or blades curved with reference to the direction of rotation. The centrifugal fans are best adapted to moving air against considerable frictional resistance. The requirements of single-phase fan duty motors .are covered by IS 996 : 1979. This standard has been prepared on the basis of IEEMA 8 : 1987 IEEMA standard for induction motors for fans used in air-conditioning and ventilation, issued by Indian Electrical and Electronics Manufacturers' Association, Bombay. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )' The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

SPECIFICATIONFORTHREE-PHASENDUCTION MOTORSFORFANSUSEDINAIR-CONDITIONING ANDVENTILATION
-1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers three-phase squirrel cage induction motors for driving fans for ventilation, airconditioning and commercial heating for voltages up to and including 11 000 V and having windings with Class E, Class B and Class F insulation ( see IS 1271 : 1985 ). 1.2 This standard does not~cover induction motors for induced draught fans, 1.3 Motors for use on systems employing nonpreferred voltage and frequency ( see 9 ) shall be considered as complying with this standard provided that these comply in all respects. The voltage and frequency for which they are designed shall be indicated on the rating plate of the motor. 2 *REFERENCE STANDARDS 2.1 The standards given in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions givenin IS 325 : 1995 and IS 1885 (Part 35 ) : 1993 shall apply. 4 CHARACTERISTICS FOR FANS 7 METHOD .OF COOLING 7.1 The methods of cooling of motors and their designations shall be in accordance with IS 6362 : 1995. 8 MATERIALS 8.1 All materials and components including insulation windings shall conform to relevant Indian Standards wherever these exist. Wherever it is not practicable to comply with this requirement, it shall be subject to agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 9 R,ATINGS 9.1 Rated Voltage 9.1.1 The preferred rated voltages shall be 415 V, 3.3 kV, 6.6 kV and 11 kV in accordance with IS 12360 : 1988. 1 shall be capable of delivering rated output with :

5.3.2 In case of continuous operation at extreme voltage limits, the temperature-rise limits specified in Table 1 of IS 12802 : 1989 shall not be exceeded by more than 1O'C. 5.3.3 Motors, when operated under the extreme conditions of voltage and frequency variation, may not necessarily have their performance in accordance with IS 325 : 1995. 5.4 It shall be assumed that the location and moisture or fumes shall not seriously interfere with the operation of the motor for driving fans. 6 TYPE OF ENCLOSURE 6.1 The motor for driving fans shall have enclosure providing one of the degrees of protection specified in IS 4691 : 1985.

4.1 Typical characteristics for axial flow fans, centrifugal fans with forward curved blades, and centrifugal fans with backward curved blades, are given in Annex B. 5 SITE CONDITIONS 5.1 The site conditions set out in 4 of IS 325 : 1995 shall apply. 5.2 In case the cooling air temperature is higher than the ambient temperature of 4O"C the variation shall be in steps of 5�C. The limits of permissible temperature-rise for different classes of insulation shall then be correspondingly reduced from the values given in 14.1 of IS ~325 : 1995, by the amount by which the cooling air temperature exceeds 4O'C. 5.3 Supply Voltage and Frequency Variation

14.2.1 The motor shall develop adequate breakaway torque for smooth and satisfactory acceleration of the load. Recommendations to control the period of starting and the requirements required to be furnished by fan manufacturers, to facilitate smooth acceleration of the load are given in Annex C. 15 OVERLOAD

IS 14377 : 1996 17.2 Some motors located inside ducts are cooled by the air stream of the driven load. The air thrown by the driven fan sewes to cool the motor body. In suqh cases, the temperature-rise of the motor is also de&ndent on the velocity of air flowing over the. motor body and the temperature-rise test on these motors can be .conducted only with the driven fan and other accessories like ducts, dampers, mounted m position. The temperature rise tests for such motors may be carried out subject to agreement between -the manufacturer and the purchaser. 18 EFFKIENCY 18.1 Efficiency 18.1.1 The efficiency shall be declared at the rated load of the motor. The method of determining the efficiency shall be in accordance with IS 4029 : 1967. The tolerance applicable to the determined values shall be in accordance with Table 1 of IS 325 : 1995. 18.2 Power Factor 18.2.1 If a statement of power factor is required, it shall be declared at the rated load of the motor. The method of determining the power factor shall be in accordance with IS 4029 : 1967. The tolerance applicable to the determined values shall be in accordance with Table 1 of IS 325 : 1995. 19 TOLERANCES 19.1 The tolerances on performance values shall be in accordance with 18.1 of IS 325 : 1995. 20 TERMINAL AND TERMINAL MARKINGS 22.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assumnce that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 23 INFORMATION TO BE GIVEN WITH ENQUIRY AND ORDER 23.1 The general information to be furnished when enquiring for or ordering the motor for fans used in air-conditioning and ventilation is given in Annex D. 24 TESTS 24.1 The provision of 23 of IS 325 : 1995 as appl~ied to squirrel cage induction motors shall be applicable. 24.2 The methods of test shall be in accordance with IS 4029 : 1967. IS 14377 : 1996 ANNEX C ( Clause 14.2.1 ) CONDITIONS FOR SMOOTH ACCELERATION C-l It is necessary to correlate the torque-speed characteristics of the motor and the driven unit, keeping in mind the starting method employed and the GD* of the driven load for the motor to develop adequate breakaway torque for smooth and satisfactory acceleration of the load. For this purpose the manufacturer of fans shall furnish the following: a) b) Speed-torque characteristics, GD2 of driven load. and OF THE LOAD DURINGSTARTING

C-2 To restrict the acceleratingperiod to a reasonable level and to control the period of starting, following is reommended:

a) Axial flow blower/fan be started undamped,
that is, with the vents open; and b) Centrifugal blowers/fans be started damped, that is, with vents closed.
